stakes.external: Something happened during the meeting. Veraine used the conversation as cover.

scene_cards.setting: Neutral meeting point — same location
scene_cards.sensory_details: Sera's voice — formal, precise, trembling with controlled emotion; Veraine's brief crack — her eyes changing, something raw behind the composure; the Force shifting during Veraine's departure — the wrongness lurching
action_beats: Sera steps forward from the group's line and faces Veraine at arm's length
Veraine flinches — quickly controlled — when Sera describes the experience of being sealed
Veraine turns and walks back toward her ship with measured steps, her crew falling in behind her
scene_cards.notes: Sera's arc: lie_challenged — she's using her principle (the lattice matters, de-structuring is violation) as a weapon, but the confrontation with Veraine shows her that principle alone doesn't protect. Veraine's sabotage objective executing under cover of the conversation.

scene_cards.mission: Aftermath aboard ship. Do not reveal the sabotage yet. Let the group process the meeting, let Ben's catalogue of Veraine and the Ash-Tithe Compact fail to settle into certainty, and let Desh begin the backward sweeps that will pay off in Chapter 17.
scene_cards.why_now: The chapter needs a decompression beat after the truce meeting, but the natural dramatic consequence belongs at the next chapter opening. This scene preserves the meeting's unresolved pressure while planting the procedural bridge to the Chapter 17 discovery.
scene_cards.conflict: Ben has more information than he can yet interpret: Veraine's register, Kael's silence, Sera's cost, the crew's tells, the ship's approach vector. The group feels worse off, but the reason is not yet visible. Desh senses an operational layer in the data and starts checking without having proof.
scene_cards.turning_point: Desh says he is running back-sweeps across the meeting window because the Ash-Tithe Compact moved like people with a job outside the conversation. Ben realizes the meeting may have been cover for something else, but there is no confirmation yet.
scene_cards.opening_hook: Back aboard the Steady Returns, the clearing dust still on their boots, nobody sits where they usually sit.
scene_cards.closing_hook: Desh starts the back-sweeps. Ben watches Veraine's ship vanish from the last passive track and knows the meeting is not finished with them.
scene_cards.emotional_trajectory: Post-meeting silence -> unsettled processing -> procedural suspicion without proof

stakes.personal: Ben may have been outplayed, but he cannot yet name how
stakes.interpersonal: Group trust sits under strain because no one can decide whether taking the meeting helped or cost them
stakes.external: If Veraine used the meeting as cover, the next loss will already be in motion before they understand it

scene_cards.setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — departure from the meeting point, tactical assessment
scene_cards.sensory_details: Clearing dust tracked across the deck plating; the ship too quiet after Veraine's measured questions; Sera standing instead of sitting, anger held below discipline; Torin trying to make warmth available and not quite reaching everyone; Kael in the corner with his hands visible and his answer still unspoken; Desh replaying passive sensor traces, not damage reports yet; Ben's memory catching on the Ash-Tithe Compact: Vess by the ramp, Pira's too-square crate, Serran's archive cylinder, Mira's fear-taught stillness
action_beats: The group boards in silence; the normal shipboard rhythm does not resume
Ben replays the meeting in fragments: Veraine's questions, Sera's answer, Kael's non-answer, and the Ash-Tithe Compact moving by function around the ship
Desh starts passive back-sweeps across the meeting window, flagging crew movement and approach-vector anomalies as suspicion rather than proof
scene_cards.notes: H16 planted — timeline collapse. Veraine's ability to be intellectually honest AND ruthlessly strategic simultaneously makes her the most dangerous kind of antagonist. She's not lying about her beliefs. She's just also willing to destroy things while explaining them.

scene_cards.mission: Assessing the damage — the timeline is now days. The group under extreme pressure. Tactical reality: they cannot stop Veraine by following. They must get to Veranthos first or simultaneously.
scene_cards.why_now: H16 resolution — the timeline collapse forces immediate tactical recalculation
scene_cards.conflict: The pressure intensifies every group friction. The wound's effect on nearby Force-sensitives amplifies emotional extremes — arguments hit harder, fear cuts deeper, doubt paralyzes.
scene_cards.turning_point: Torin standing in the doorway: 'We need to talk about what happens when we get there.' His voice calm, warm, decided. Ben's stomach drops.
scene_cards.opening_hook: Desh converts the seal degradation rate to hours and posts the number on the cockpit display. It's small enough to memorize. Nobody wants to.
scene_cards.closing_hook: Torin's tone. Ben has heard that tone before. Jacen used it in the weeks before the worst things happened — the certainty of someone who has already decided and is now only negotiating the announcement.
scene_cards.emotional_trajectory: Urgent tactical focus -> group pressure cracking -> Torin's ominous calm

stakes.personal: Ben hearing the Jacen pattern in Torin's voice — the recognition crystallizing
stakes.interpersonal: Torin separating from the group emotionally even while physically present
stakes.external: Days until Veraine reaches Veranthos

scene_cards.setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — cockpit and common area, hyperspace toward Veranthos
scene_cards.sensory_details: Desh's countdown display; the wrongness now a constant pressure, like altitude sickness; arguments flaring hotter than they should — the wound amplifying emotional extremes; Torin's silhouette in the doorway
action_beats: Desh converts the seal degradation rate to hours and posts the countdown on the cockpit display
Ben paces the common area while assigning approach tasks — nerves converting to motion
Torin stands in the doorway and speaks with the calm warm tone that drops Ben's stomach
scene_cards.notes: H17 planted — Torin's 'We need to talk.' The most ominous hook in the book because it's delivered with warmth. Torin's arc: lie_deepened — his certainty is now a decision, not just a philosophy.

scene_cards.mission: The group under pressure — tempers flare as the wound amplifies tensions. Sera and Kael clash over tactics. Desh mediates practically. The small ship feels like a pressure cooker.
scene_cards.why_now: The wound's amplification effect on nearby Force-sensitives turns normal disagreements into potential fractures
scene_cards.conflict: Sera wants to reinforce the seal with traditional Jedi methods. Kael points out those methods were built by the people who created the problem. The argument escalates beyond what either would normally say — the wound pushing.
scene_cards.turning_point: Ben feels the amplification effect for the first time — his own anger at Kael's cynicism is disproportionate, and he catches himself mid-sentence. The wound isn't just a cosmic problem. It's in this room.
scene_cards.opening_hook: The argument starts about hyperspace routes. It stops being about hyperspace routes within thirty seconds.
scene_cards.closing_hook: After the fight, silence. Desh brings everyone something to eat without being asked. Nobody thanks him. He doesn't expect them to. The silence after the argument is more informative than the argument itself.
scene_cards.emotional_trajectory: Simmering tension -> explosive argument -> exhausted silence

stakes.personal: Ben recognizing the wound's influence on his own emotional state
stakes.interpersonal: Group cohesion fracturing under external psychic pressure
stakes.external: If the wound can amplify their tensions, it's doing the same to every Force-sensitive in range

scene_cards.setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — common area, cramped and overheated
scene_cards.sensory_details: The ship too warm; recycled air stale; voices bouncing off metal walls; Ben's own anger — hot, disproportionate, recognizably amplified; Desh's food offerings — practical kindness in the absence of resolution
action_beats: Sera slams her palm on the nav console mid-argument — the sound silencing the cockpit for a breath
Ben catches himself mid-sentence as his own anger spikes disproportionate — the wound pushing
Desh brings food to each person without being asked, navigating the silent aftermath
scene_cards.notes: The wound's amplification effect is critical — it makes the interpersonal drama physically real, not just character conflict. Arguments are louder, fears deeper, doubts more paralyzing. This isn't possession — it's pressurization.

scene_cards.opening_hook: The outpost looks normal from approach. The Knight who meets them at the landing pad does not look normal. His eyes are too wide and his hands are too still — the careful control of someone holding themselves together.
scene_cards.closing_hook: Torin watches the suffering Knights with an expression that is not compassion. It is calculation. He is measuring the cost of inaction against the cost of his proposed solution.

Ben's response to helplessness (leading without controlling) shows her a kind of leadership Gavran never demonstrated.

scene_cards.why_now: H21 resolution — the Codex note becomes a plan. The intellectual heart of Part 4.
scene_cards.conflict: The theory requires three distinct Force traditions to create resonance — Jedi (Sera), modern Jedi with Skywalker lineage perception (Ben), and Sith-trained (Kael). It has never been tested. It might kill them. And it requires Kael's full, willing participation.
scene_cards.turning_point: Sera's new truth demonstrated: instead of insisting on the traditional Jedi approach, she engages with the resonance theory on its own terms. Principled flexibility — adapting her framework without abandoning her principles.
scene_cards.opening_hook: The Codex notes spread between them, Ben and Sera work through the theory with the focused intensity of two people building a bomb they intend to defuse themselves.
scene_cards.closing_hook: The plan works — in theory. It requires three Force traditions. They have two who are willing. Kael is the variable. Without him, there is no resonance. Without resonance, there is only Torin's sacrifice or Veraine's destruction.
scene_cards.emotional_trajectory: Intense intellectual work -> breakthrough -> the dependency on Kael's choice

stakes.personal: Ben and Sera working as true partners for the first time
stakes.interpersonal: Sera's arc advancing — flexibility without abandonment of principle
stakes.external: The resonance theory is the only alternative to Torin's unilateral sacrifice

scene_cards.setting: Veranthos — camp, working through the night with Codex materials
scene_cards.sensory_details: Codex fragments and archive data spread across every surface; the wound's pull from below — constant, patient; Sera's archaic notation alongside Ben's modern analysis; Desh providing logistical reality checks
action_beats: Ben and Sera spread Codex notes across every flat surface in the camp workspace and work through the resonance theory side by side
Sera adapts archaic notation to match Ben's modern Force framework — her handwriting flowing alongside his on the same datapad
Desh provides logistical reality checks from the supply manifest while they calculate resonance requirements

scene_cards.notes: R12 — the lattice resonance solution articulated. Sera's arc: new_truth_demonstrated — she's adapting, not abandoning. The shift from 'Skywalker' to 'Ben' may begin here, subtle.

scene_cards.mission: The amplification array understood — Desh realizes what Veraine has been building across the Corridor. Each repurposed node is an antenna in a network aimed at the Scar. The group didn't recognize the pattern because they were looking at nodes individually.
scene_cards.why_now: The tactical picture completes — understanding both Veraine's plan and how to counter it
scene_cards.conflict: The array requires a critical mass of approximately eight repurposed nodes to function. If Desh can disable three critical nodes, Veraine drops below threshold. But the nodes are guarded by her crew, and Desh would have to operate solo.
scene_cards.turning_point: Desh volunteers for the sabotage mission before anyone asks. 'That's my job. Let the Force-users do the Force thing. I'll handle the part that requires hands.' His arc completing — from obligation to chosen commitment.
scene_cards.opening_hook: Desh stares at the Corridor map with the amplification overlay and his expression goes very still. 'I know what she built. I know how to break it.'
scene_cards.closing_hook: Two plans, both dependent on trust: the resonance trio needs Kael; the sabotage needs Desh alone against armed opposition. Both plans fail without both parts.
scene_cards.emotional_trajectory: Tactical revelation -> Desh's willing commitment -> the interlocking dependency

stakes.personal: Desh's arc payoff — choosing the dangerous task freely
stakes.interpersonal: The group becoming a genuine team through voluntary specialization
stakes.external: The two-pronged plan is the only path to defeating Veraine AND saving the seal

scene_cards.setting: Veranthos — camp, tactical planning with Corridor data
scene_cards.sensory_details: The amplification array visible on the map — a web of repurposed nodes pointing at Veranthos; Desh's professional assessment overlaid with personal resolve; dawn approaching — they're running out of darkness
action_beats: Desh stares at the Corridor map with the amplification overlay and his expression goes clinical — intelligence analyst, not friend
Desh traces the three critical nodes on the map and outlines his solo sabotage approach
Desh volunteers before anyone asks — straightening from the map table with his decision already made
scene_cards.notes: Desh's arc: new_truth_demonstrated — volunteers for the most dangerous physical task without being asked. The former GAG operative finding genuine purpose.

scene_cards.mission: Ben must now convince Kael. The plan requires three traditions — and Kael's Sith-trained contribution is the piece that can't be substituted. Ben knows he can't command this. Kael must choose freely.
scene_cards.why_now: The plan is built but incomplete without Kael. The thematic argument demands that Kael's participation be voluntary.
scene_cards.conflict: Ben prepares to ask Kael — not command, not manipulate, not guilt-trip. Ask. The hardest thing for a Skywalker: trusting someone else's free choice when everything depends on it.
scene_cards.turning_point: Ben acknowledges to himself: if Kael says no, the plan fails. And that has to be acceptable. Forcing Kael would repeat every institution that ever used him. The answer has to be free or it isn't an answer.
scene_cards.opening_hook: Kael sits at the camp's edge with his legs over the ridgeline, facing the valley and the Scar below. He doesn't turn when Ben approaches — he felt him coming.
scene_cards.closing_hook: Kael's question: 'Why should I believe this one is different?' Not hostile. Not cynical. Genuine. The final holdout before the plan can execute.
scene_cards.emotional_trajectory: Steeling resolve -> the approach -> Kael's devastating question

stakes.personal: Ben learning to lead through invitation rather than command
stakes.interpersonal: Ben and Kael — the Jedi and the Sith-trained, asking each other for trust
stakes.external: Without Kael, no resonance. Without resonance, Torin's sacrifice or Veraine's destruction.

scene_cards.setting: Veranthos — camp edge, overlooking the valley and the Scar
scene_cards.sensory_details: The Scar visible below — a seam in reality; Kael's Force presence — guarded but not hostile; the wrongness between them, making the conversation harder than it should be; first light touching the ridgelines
action_beats: Kael sits at the camp's edge with legs over the ridgeline, facing the Scar below
Ben sits down beside Kael and presents the resonance plan — theory, requirements, risks, his specific role — holding nothing back
Kael turns the question over in silence, his fingers pulling at the grass beside him
scene_cards.notes: H22 planted — Kael's question: 'Why should I believe this one is different?' The final character holdout. Ben's leadership through invitation, not command, is the thematic argument in action.

scene_cards.mission: Ben presents the resonance plan to Kael fully — the theory, the requirements, the risks, and what Kael's specific contribution would be. No manipulation, no half-truths. The whole picture.
scene_cards.why_now: H22 payoff — answering Kael's question with action, not rhetoric
scene_cards.conflict: Kael's challenge: every institution that has ever asked him to serve has also used him. The Sith conscripted him. The Jedi captured him and sealed him as infrastructure. Now another Jedi is asking him to contribute his Sith-trained abilities to a collective effort. Why should this be different?
scene_cards.turning_point: Ben answers Kael's question honestly: 'Because I'm asking. Not ordering. And if you say no, I will not make you. This works or fails on your free choice. That's what makes it different from everything that came before.'
scene_cards.opening_hook: Ben tells Kael everything. The theory. The math. The risk. The part where it's never been tested. The part where it might kill them. The part where it won't work without him.
scene_cards.closing_hook: Kael sits with it. A long time. The wrongness presses down. When he speaks, his voice is dry, level, and the driest it's ever been: 'How sure are you this will work?' Ben: 'Not very.' Kael: 'Points for honesty.'
scene_cards.emotional_trajectory: Honest presentation -> Kael's challenge -> the honest answer that works because it's honest

stakes.personal: Ben demonstrating the new truth — trust rather than control
stakes.interpersonal: Kael being treated as a person with a choice, not an asset to deploy
stakes.external: The resonance plan's viability rests on this conversation

scene_cards.setting: Veranthos — camp edge, dawn fully established now
scene_cards.sensory_details: Morning light on the valley — beautiful and wrong; the Scar visible below; Kael's face — the careful blankness of someone who is feeling too much to show any of it; Ben's open hands — no weapons, no manipulation, just the plan
action_beats: Ben lays out the resonance theory on a datapad between them — the math, the requirements, the untested risk
Ben holds his hands open while presenting — no weapons, no manipulation, just the plan
Kael's face shifts from careful blankness to something new when Ben admits the odds
scene_cards.notes: The honest answer ('Not very') working BECAUSE it's honest is the thematic argument in miniature. Kael has been lied to by experts. The truth is what he doesn't expect.

scene_cards.mission: Kael's internal processing — Ben watches but gives him space. Kael walks to the edge and stares at the Scar. His decision is not about the plan's probability of success. It's about whether choosing is different from being chosen.
scene_cards.why_now: The space between the ask and the answer — Kael must process this without pressure
scene_cards.conflict: Kael's Lie (conviction is a trap, the safest place is outside the fight) vs. his Need (choosing to care is the only way to stop being a tool). The crisis has made neutrality impossible — refusal to choose has become complicity.
scene_cards.turning_point: Kael looks at Desh working on equipment — the non-Force-user who chose to be here, who chose danger for reasons that aren't about power or destiny or conviction. Just... purpose. Kael realizes that Desh is the freest person in the group.
scene_cards.opening_hook: Kael walks away. Not leaving — thinking. Ben forces himself to let him go. Trust means accepting the possibility of no.
scene_cards.closing_hook: Kael turns back. His face is different — not the careful blankness, not the dry detachment. Something new. Something that looks, against all odds, like choice.
scene_cards.emotional_trajectory: Waiting -> Kael's internal processing (observed externally) -> the visible change

stakes.personal: Kael's arc climax — choosing to care after a lifetime of enforced indifference
stakes.interpersonal: The Kael/Desh parallel — the non-Force-user modeling genuine freedom
stakes.external: Without Kael's commitment, the resonance fails

scene_cards.setting: Veranthos — camp, Kael walking to the edge, looking down at the Scar, looking at Desh, looking inward
scene_cards.sensory_details: Kael's Force presence — shifting, the guarded walls lowering for the first time; Desh working on equipment, unaware he's being watched; the Scar below, patient, waiting; Kael's footsteps returning
action_beats: Kael walks away from Ben toward the ridge edge — not leaving, processing
Kael watches Desh working on equipment from a distance — the non-Force-user who chose to be here
Kael turns back toward the group, his stride different — less careful, more deliberate
scene_cards.notes: Kael's arc: lie_confronted — the crisis forces the choice. His observation of Desh is the key: chosen commitment is different from conscripted service. Desh models what Kael has never experienced.

scene_cards.mission: Kael commits — 'If this kills me, I want it on record that I volunteered. First time for everything.' The resonance trio is complete. The plan can execute.
scene_cards.why_now: Kael's decision — the final character commitment before the climax
scene_cards.conflict: The commitment is real — and so is the vulnerability. Kael has never voluntarily put himself at risk for others. The humor covers the magnitude of what he's doing.
scene_cards.turning_point: Kael's line: 'If this kills me, I want it on record that I volunteered. First time for everything.' Dry, self-aware, and the most important thing he's ever said. He's choosing. Not conscripted, not captured, not sealed. Choosing.
scene_cards.opening_hook: Kael walks back to the group. His stride is different — less careful, more deliberate. Ben watches him approach and knows the answer before he speaks.
scene_cards.closing_hook: The group moves toward the wound source — three Force-users and one non-Force-user, walking toward something unprecedented. Ben feels Sera's and Kael's Force presences beside him. Different. Complementary. Not yet a chord. But the notes are there.
scene_cards.emotional_trajectory: The commitment -> group relief and resolve -> the march toward the endgame

stakes.personal: Kael's arc payoff — chosen commitment, the antithesis of his Lie
stakes.interpersonal: The resonance trio formed — Ben, Sera, Kael. Three traditions, three wounds, one attempt.
stakes.external: The climax is imminent

scene_cards.setting: Veranthos — camp, then movement toward the valley
scene_cards.sensory_details: Kael's stride — deliberate, not careful; his voice delivering the line — dry, level, the humor covering something raw; three Force presences aligning — not harmonized yet but adjacent, complementary; the valley below, waiting
action_beats: Kael walks back to the group with a stride that's changed — less careful, more deliberate, decided
Kael delivers his line with the driest voice Ben has heard — the humor covering something enormous
The group moves together toward the valley — three Force-users and one non-Force-user walking toward something unprecedented
promises_paid: Kael's detachment breaks into chosen commitment (PP09)
scene_cards.notes: Kael's arc: new_truth_demonstrated. Kael/Veraine parallel resolution — same wound as Veraine, opposite choice. She chose destruction; he chooses participation. The 'first time for everything' line should be one of the book's most memorable.

scene_cards.mission: Approach to the valley epicenter. Torin visible on the ridgeline — already descending, already deploying the technique at personal scale. Final Ben/Torin exchange across distance.
scene_cards.why_now: The three-way convergence beginning — all parties moving toward the Scar simultaneously
scene_cards.conflict: Ben's last attempt to reach Torin across the distance — through the Force, through words, through shared experience. Torin hears him. Responds with genuine affection. And keeps walking.
scene_cards.turning_point: Torin's voice, carried across the valley: 'I understand what you're trying to do, Ben. It's the right impulse. But some problems only have one solution.' The use of 'Ben' — not 'Skywalker' — carries warmth that makes it worse.
scene_cards.opening_hook: The valley opens below them. Three-way geometry: Veraine at the Scar, Torin descending the ridgeline, the resonance group at mid-valley. Desh already gone — heading to the first amplification node.
scene_cards.closing_hook: Torin begins the technique. Ben feels it — the lattice near Torin leaning toward him and dissolving. A pulling, a suction. Like standing next to a drain. The climax begins.
scene_cards.emotional_trajectory: Desperate hope for Torin -> the failed appeal's grief -> the technique activating

stakes.personal: Ben's last chance to save Torin — and the acceptance that he can't force it
stakes.interpersonal: The Ben/Torin relationship's final exchange — genuine love across irreconcilable choices
stakes.external: The three-way convergence at the Scar is about to collide

scene_cards.setting: Veranthos — valley approach, ridgeline visible, the Scar at the valley floor
scene_cards.sensory_details: The valley's geometry — ridgelines, slopes, the Scar at the lowest point; Torin's descending figure; the technique activating — the lattice leaning toward Torin, dissolving, a cliff edge between structured and unstructured Force; Veraine's ritual visible at the Scar as distant distortion
action_beats: The group descends into the valley in formation while Desh splits off toward the first amplification node
Ben calls across the valley to Torin and Torin pauses on the ridgeline, turning to listen
Torin begins the technique and the lattice near him leans inward and dissolves — a pulling, a suction
scene_cards.notes: Torin using 'Ben' instead of a title or surname carries enormous weight. The failed appeal should hurt because it comes from love, not conflict. Torin isn't rejecting Ben — he's rejecting Ben's approach while admiring Ben's character.

scene_cards.mission: Veraine's ritual building at the Scar — amplified by the repurposed node network. The wound responding, the Scar widening. The three forces converging: Veraine at the epicenter, Torin descending, the resonance trio at mid-valley.
scene_cards.why_now: The climax infrastructure is in motion — all three forces active simultaneously
scene_cards.conflict: The physical environment deteriorating as all three operations stress the lattice. The wrongness becoming acute — not just uncomfortable but dangerous. The wound amplifying emotions, making concentration nearly impossible.
scene_cards.turning_point: Ben feels all three operations in the Force simultaneously: Veraine's ritual (calculated, amplified, aimed at the Scar), Torin's technique (personal, immediate, the lattice dissolving around him), and the beginning of their own resonance (discordant, uncertain). Three operations pulling the Force in three different directions.
scene_cards.opening_hook: Ben watches the Scar widen — a centimeter, maybe two. Enough to be visible. Enough to be terrifying.
scene_cards.closing_hook: Ben: 'Now.' He reaches for Sera and Kael through the Force. Three traditions. Three wounds. One chance.
scene_cards.emotional_trajectory: Environmental overwhelm -> focus through chaos -> the call to begin

stakes.personal: Ben committing to the resonance — no more preparation, no more theory
stakes.interpersonal: Three people trusting each other with their lives and their Force connections
stakes.external: Three operations competing at the wound site — only one can succeed

scene_cards.setting: Veranthos — mid-valley position, Scar visible, Torin visible, Veraine's ritual visible
scene_cards.sensory_details: The Scar widening; Veraine's ritual — a distortion at the Scar's base, calculated and focused; Torin's technique — the lattice dissolving around him as he descends, a moving void; the resonance starting point — three Force presences reaching for each other, discordant
action_beats: Ben watches the Scar widen by centimeters and feels all three operations pulling the Force in different directions
Sera and Kael take positions flanking Ben, hands outstretched, the resonance formation assembling
Ben reaches for Sera and Kael through the Force and speaks the word: 'Now.'
scene_cards.notes: The three operations coexisting creates the climax's physical texture. Each is a different type of Force manipulation, and Ben can feel all three. The sensory vocabulary should be at maximum density here.

scene_cards.mission: The resonance starts discordant — three traditions that have never combined. Ben, Sera, Kael join hands. Three notes that don't form a chord. It feels clumsy, unstable.
scene_cards.why_now: The resonance attempt's first moments — failure before success, earned difficulty
scene_cards.conflict: The three Force traditions resist combination — not because of hostility but because they're structurally incompatible. Jedi lattice-work, pre-Ruusan Jedi discipline, and Sith-trained Force manipulation operate on different frequencies.
scene_cards.turning_point: The discordance is overwhelming. Ben's instinct to control kicks in — he tries to lead, to harmonize the three notes by force of will. It doesn't work. His Lie, again: control as safety. The resonance resists being commanded.
scene_cards.opening_hook: Three hands linked. Three Force traditions touching. The sound of it — in the Force — is like three instruments playing in different keys simultaneously.
scene_cards.closing_hook: It's not working. The discordance is worsening. Veraine's ritual is building power. Torin's void is expanding. And the resonance is falling apart. Ben is trying too hard. He's leading when he should be listening.
scene_cards.emotional_trajectory: Determined attempt -> frustration at failure -> the recognition that control is the problem

stakes.personal: Ben's Lie making one last stand — his instinct to control sabotaging the resonance
stakes.interpersonal: Three people failing to harmonize because one of them is trying to dominate
stakes.external: The other two operations are succeeding while theirs fails

scene_cards.setting: Veranthos — mid-valley, hands linked, the Scar visible, the valley in chaos
scene_cards.sensory_details: The discordance — three Force textures clashing; Ben's instinct to control manifesting as Force pressure; Sera's tradition rigid and defined; Kael's tradition fluid and sharp; the three failing to combine; sweat, strain, the wound pressing
action_beats: Ben links hands with Sera and Kael and the three Force traditions collide — discordant, unstable, wrong
Ben tries to lead the resonance by force of will and feels it resist — his control instinct sabotaging the harmony
Sweat rolls down Ben's temples as the discordance worsens and the other two operations grow stronger around them
scene_cards.notes: The failure-before-success is essential. The resonance CAN'T work while Ben is trying to control it. His Lie making one last attempt. The breakthrough comes in Chapter 25 when he lets go.

scene_cards.mission: The resonance catches — Ben stops trying to control it. The breakthrough comes when he lets go and listens instead of leading. The three notes find their own relationship — emergent, not commanded.
scene_cards.why_now: The climactic breakthrough — Ben's arc completing through action. The new truth demonstrated: trust, surrender of control, orchestration rather than possession.
scene_cards.conflict: Ben's internal battle: every Skywalker instinct screams to take control, to force the harmony. His need demands the opposite. He lets go.
scene_cards.turning_point: Ben stops leading and starts listening. The three traditions — instead of being forced into alignment — find their own relationship. An emergent harmony, a chord built from notes that shouldn't fit but do. The resonance catches. Warmth after cold.
scene_cards.opening_hook: The discordance is reaching critical. Sera's jaw is set. Kael's hands are trembling. Ben is trying everything he knows and nothing is working. Then he thinks of Desh — the man who leads by making space for other people's competence. And he lets go.
scene_cards.closing_hook: The resonance catches. The warmth is physical — not metaphorical. After the bone-deep cold of de-structuring, after months of the wrongness, the return of structure feels like hearing a note you didn't know you were part of. Relief, not triumph.
scene_cards.emotional_trajectory: Desperate control -> the moment of surrender -> the breakthrough warmth

stakes.personal: Ben's arc culminating — trust and surrender as strength
stakes.interpersonal: Three traditions harmonizing — the thematic argument made physical
stakes.external: The resonance works. The question is whether it's enough.

scene_cards.setting: Veranthos — mid-valley, hands linked, the resonance catching
scene_cards.sensory_details: The three notes finding their relationship — not any single tradition's structure but something emergent; warmth returning through the Force after cold; the lattice reforming not as rigid grid but as living tissue — flexible, dynamic; relief like breathing after nearly drowning
action_beats: Sera sets her jaw and Kael's hands tremble as the discordance reaches critical — the resonance failing
Ben releases his grip on control — stops leading, starts listening — and the three traditions find their own relationship
