spatial_logistics.veraine: At the Scar (valley floor epicenter), performing amplified ritual to open the wound. Crew members posted at critical nearby amplification nodes as guards.
spatial_logistics.torin: Approaching from the ridgeline, descending toward the Scar. Personal-scale technique creates de-structured zone around his body as he moves. He IS the equipment.
spatial_logistics.resonance_trio: Ben, Sera, and Kael at mid-valley — close enough to reach the wound with the resonance, far enough to avoid Veraine's ritual zone and Torin's de-structured field.
spatial_logistics.desh: Off-site. Running solo infiltration/sabotage operation against crew-guarded amplification nodes. Former GAG operative vs. mundane opposition under extreme time pressure.

sequence.chapter_24: Setup and failed appeal. Group arrives at valley's outer edge. Torin already in the valley. Final Ben/Torin exchange fails. Torin begins the technique. Veraine's ritual building. Ben calls resonance: 'Now.'
sequence.chapter_25: Three-way collision. Resonance starts discordant — three traditions that have never combined. Torin's technique works immediately (known quantity). Veraine's ritual powerful (amplified by network). Desh starts disabling nodes. Veraine's amplification drops. Resonance catches when Ben stops trying to control it — lets Sera and Kael contribute as equals.
sequence.chapter_26: Resolution. Veraine's ritual fails (two-stage: Desh removes amplification, resonance produces unmodelable emergence). Torin partially succeeds but is consumed — pulled free by Sera, alive but diminished. New seal stabilizes: dynamic, harmonic, requiring periodic renewal.

climax_mechanics.what_breaks_veraine: Two-stage defeat. Stage 1 (physical/tactical): Desh disables three critical amplification nodes, dropping Veraine below the threshold where her ritual can breach the wound. She's strong alone but not strong enough — the seal was the work of thirteen anchors. Stage 2 (philosophical/structural): The resonance produces an emergent pattern from three traditions that Veraine's analytical framework can't model. She planned for single-tradition opposition (Jedi resealing with old methods). She didn't plan for synthesis. She identifies the Jedi and pre-Ruusan components and starts building a counter-pattern, but Kael's Sith-trained component adds the unintegrable variable — not because it's more powerful, but because its relationship to the other traditions is something her framework can't compute. She was right about the problem (the light/dark binary is limiting) and catastrophically wrong about the solution (harmonize, don't eliminate).
climax_mechanics.why_torin_isnt_stopped: The group lets him go because physically overriding his agency would repeat the exact pattern the book condemns — Gavran deciding for Sera, Jacen deciding what's necessary. Each character's silence has distinct texture rooted in their arc: Ben (failed to stop this pattern with Jacen, has no alternative yet), Sera (was the person whose agency was overridden — cannot do to Torin what Gavran did to her), Kael (spent his life being redirected — won't do it to someone else), Desh (breaks silence with operational pragmatism — redirects group from paralysis to action).

kael_veraine_parallel.description: Kael and Veraine share identical histories of institutional conscription and exploitation — both born on worlds controlled by factions they didn't choose, both conscripted into Force training, both captured by Gavran's forces, both repurposed as anchors in the seal. Their parallel tests the thematic question from the perspective of the used rather than the user. Same wound, opposite scar tissue: Kael responds with exhaustion and withdrawal (conviction is a trap, passivity is safety); Veraine responds with fury and purpose (the system that used me is the disease, I'll tear it down). The book's answer is neither — it's reconstruction through relationship, embodied by Kael's free choice to participate in the resonance.

touchpoints.description: Both backstories emerge during the fortress awakening. The reader can see the parallel before the characters do. The empty chamber and the occupied chambers tell complementary stories.
Veraine's deliberate message at the Brotherhood outpost is aimed at Kael specifically — speaking to the one person whose history mirrors hers. Kael reads it and says nothing. Ben notices his silence.

The truce meeting. Veraine makes her pitch directly to Kael. Her argument is strongest when aimed at him because she knows his experience validates her thesis. The tension is real — the reader should feel the pull.

At the Jedi outpost, Kael observes that the Knights 'built their identity on the lattice.' His perspective diverges from Veraine's: she would say the lattice is the problem; Kael says the dependence on a single framework is the problem. He's arriving at the resonance answer before Ben articulates it.

Kael commits to the resonance. Same wound as Veraine, opposite choice. She chose destruction; he chooses participation. 'If this kills me, I want it on record that I volunteered. First time for everything.'

political_landscape.jedi_order_47aby: The post-FotJ Jedi Order has survived multiple existential crises in rapid succession — the Swarm War, Jacen's fall, Luke's exile, the Lost Tribe, Abeloth. Experienced but exhausted. They've proven they can survive anything — and the galaxy has started wondering whether the crises follow the Jedi rather than the other way around. Luke is Grand Master but the role carries political weight he never wanted. Internal fault lines: generational tension, questions about the Order's institutional model, a younger generation (Ben's) that has known nothing but crisis.
political_landscape.galactic_alliance_relations: Cooperative but wary. The memory of Jacen Solo as Chief of State and Sith Lord simultaneously is less than two decades old. Politicians who respect, tolerate, or resent Jedi influence. The Reformations are the Order's standard defense against political criticism: 'We reformed. We have checks and balances. We serve, we don't rule.' If that defense is undermined — if the Reformations are revealed as penance rather than principle — the political ground shifts.
political_landscape.implications_for_ben: Ben's decision to withhold truth (Chapter 15) and then reveal it (Chapter 28) carries real institutional risk. Disclosure reframes the Order's foundational narrative: the Reformations weren't principled reform, they were damage control. Not because Luke lied (he didn't know) but because the institution's self-understanding was built on amnesia. Ben's GAG history gives him a lens for recognizing institutional self-preservation — he's seen what institutions do when they prioritize survival over truth. His Chapter 28 decision is informed by having lived through institutional corruption once already.

relationship_arcs.want: To be father and son without the Order between them.
relationship_arcs.need: To choose the private relationship actively, not wait for circumstances to permit it.

drafting_specimens.description: Canonical-text fixtures for passages the drafter must render verbatim. Pinning these preserves in-book references (e.g. the caldera warning) across chapter boundaries and across runs.

gavran_final_log.context: Recovered from Gavran's Chamber (fortress Level 4). The last entry in his personal monitoring log. Trails off mid-sentence. Ben reads it at the end of Chapter 4.
gavran_final_log.text: Day ~712 post-Ruusan. Anchor count: thirteen remaining, including myself. Ven has stopped responding to the stasis interrogatives — his Force presence still reads on the network, but I no longer register the person. I have been the keystone for forty years and I am no longer certain whether what holds the seal is my will or the habit of my will. If this recording is found: the containment was a field expedient. It was never meant to be permanent. Someone has to decide what replaces it before the last anchor—

ankhural_resonance_passage.context: The Ankhural Codex fragment Ben finds in Chapter 22 after Torin's departure. Seeds the climactic resonance solution.
ankhural_resonance_passage.text: The lattice is a structure and structures fail alone. Any single tradition that seeks to reinforce it will impose its own shape on the reinforcement, and the lattice will register that imposition as further injury. But three traditions in concert may produce a harmonic reinforcement no single tradition could — the lattice reading the overlap, not the assertion, as its native state. We lacked the will or the trust to attempt it.

maetha_warning.context: Delivered via Maetha's archived holocron at her training facility (Chapter 12). The most important single line of foreshadowing in the book. Fragments should echo in later chapters, especially 'replaces you.'
maetha_warning.text: The caldera does not consume you. It replaces you. You will still breathe. You will still speak. The people who loved you will not recognize what breathes and speaks, and you will no longer have the language to explain why.

perimeter_facility_message.context: Automated message transmitted from the Gavran-era perimeter facility Ben and Desh find in Chapter 3. Short, coded, urgent. Includes the coordinates to the fortress.
perimeter_facility_message.text: Relay authorization: Jedi Lord Command, Ruusan-era. Message repeats: The seal is failing. Anchor count below critical. Coordinates follow. If you can hear this, you are already inside the contingency perimeter and the contingency is you.

calendar.description: In-story calendar anchors for the Ruusan Atonement. Used for continuity checks between scenes and for chapter-to-chapter elapsed-time references.
calendar.journey_duration: approximately 42 standard days from departure (Ch1) to the climactic events at Veranthos (Ch25-26), followed by a week of return travel.
calendar.note: Galactic Standard Calendar convention per Legends EU: Nelona and Kelona are months 4 and 5 of the standard year; Selona is month 6. Characters reference events by month + day, never by ABY designation (ABY is fan/historian shorthand, not in-universe).
